title: Chemical Changes
seo_title: Secondary 2 Science: Chemical Changes Worksheets (Lower Secondary Science with Answers)
standard_text: Identify chemical changes as changes in which new substances are formed and represent them with word equations; recognise that atoms are rearranged and mass is conserved; recognise combustion, thermal decomposition, oxidation (rusting and respiration) and neutralisation; investigate chemical changes caused by mixing, heating, light, oxygen and electric current; recognise their benefits and harmful effects (summary of the MOE Lower Secondary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 2 science worksheets for Singapore students on chemical changes: physical vs chemical change, word equations, combustion, thermal decomposition, rusting and conservation of mass. With answers.
key_big: A chemical change makes new substances.
key_sub: Atoms are rearranged, so mass is conserved.
body_html:
How to think about it

In a chemical change, new substances form. Atoms are rearranged, so mass is conserved.

  • Write word equations: reactants → products, e.g. magnesium + oxygen → magnesium oxide.
  • Combustion (burning in oxygen), thermal decomposition (breaking down on heating), oxidation (rusting, respiration), neutralisation (acid + alkali).
  • Chemical changes can be caused by mixing, heating, light, oxygen and electric current.
  • Some are useful (cooking, respiration); some are harmful (rusting, food going bad).
Example

12 g of magnesium reacts with 8 g of oxygen. Mass of magnesium oxide?

Mass is conserved

Answer: 20 g

Example

calcium carbonate → calcium oxide + carbon dioxide. Type?

One substance breaks down on heating

Answer: thermal decomposition

Common mistakes

  • Calling melting or dissolving a chemical change. No new substance forms.
  • Thinking mass is lost when a gas is made. In a sealed flask the mass stays the same.
  • Saying rusting needs only water. It needs oxygen and water.
  • Saying new atoms are made. Atoms are only rearranged.

faq.q: How can you tell a chemical change has happened?
faq.a: A new substance forms. Signs include a colour change, a gas given off, a solid forming, or heat and light given out.

faq.q: Why is mass conserved in a reaction?
faq.a: Atoms are only rearranged; none are created or destroyed.

faq.q: What are the main types of chemical change?
faq.a: Combustion, thermal decomposition, oxidation (such as rusting and respiration) and neutralisation.

items.q: Is ice melting a physical change or a chemical change?
c: a chemical change, because it looks different
a chemical change, because a new substance is formed
a physical change, because no new substance is formed
items.e: Look for a new substance: a colour change, gas, heat or light that cannot easily be reversed.

items.q: What happens to atoms in a chemical reaction?
c: They are rearranged to form new substances; none are created or destroyed.
items.e: This is why mass is conserved.

items.q: What happens to atoms in a chemical reaction?
